how: The Dow peaked eight weeks before the Nasdaq and ten before the S&P 500. By 10 March it was 15% below this level.

t: Fed raises to 5.75%; 10-year yield falls below 2-year
how: Dow −38, Nasdaq +22: money moved into technology. The yield curve stayed inverted until 28 December 2000.
Nasdaq +1.76 points on the day; the Dow fell 82 and was 15.3% below its own peak. The Nasdaq fell 77.9% from here.
Relief rally: S&P 500 +2.6%, Dow +227; the Nasdaq reversed a 143-point loss to close +102.
Fourth straight record, by 0.11 point. The Nasdaq was already below its peak. The index fell 49.1% from here in 637 sessions.

t: Tiger Management closes its funds to outside investors
how: A fund that had bet against the bubble gave up at the top. Nasdaq −4.0% that day. Date taken from secondary citations of the press.
Nasdaq −7.6% while the Dow rose 300 points: sellers of technology bought old-economy shares. The ruling came after the close.
The Dow was down about 500 points at its worst and closed −57. One strategist called a bottom that day.

t: Hot CPI and margin calls: Nasdaq −9.7%, S&P 500 −5.8%
how: Nasdaq −25% on the week. The S&P 500’s first close 10% below its high (−11.1%). The next two sessions were the Nasdaq’s largest point gains to that date.

t: Fed raises 0.50 point to 6.50%: the last rise
how: Expected, and stocks rose: Nasdaq +3%, S&P 500 +0.9%. The Nasdaq then fell five days running to its spring low.
Nasdaq −5.9% on the day; S&P 500 10.1% below its peak. The Nasdaq rose 35.1% over the next eight weeks.
Up 35.1% from 23 May and still 15.3% below the March record. The S&P 500 was 1.1% below its own.
The Nasdaq was 16% below its peak the same day. Tame data led to comment that the Fed was finished. The lasting decline began here.
Warned after the close on 21 September. Record volume in Intel; the Dow recovered a 140-point loss to close +82. First of a run of warnings.
Nasdaq −5.6%, S&P 500 −2.4%. Optical-equipment customers were cutting orders and holding excess stock.
Nasdaq −5.4%, S&P 500 −1.6%. The dispute lasted until 12 December and the ruling that ended it brought no rally.

t: Greenspan says growth has slowed: Nasdaq +10.5%
how: The Nasdaq’s largest one-day gain to that date; S&P 500 +3.9%. No cut followed for four weeks.

t: Fed holds at 6.50% but now warns of weakness
how: The market wanted a cut: Nasdaq −4.3%, then −7.1% the next day. The Nasdaq ended 2000 down 39%.
Between meetings, the day after a factory survey at its lowest since 1991. S&P 500 +5.0% on record volume. The rally lasted three weeks.
Up 24.8% from 2 January. A second cut on 31 January was sold. The Nasdaq fell 42.7% from here to 4 April.

t: Cisco misses for the first time in over six years
how: Reported after the close on 6 February. Cisco −13%, Nasdaq −2.1%. Nortel, Dell and Hewlett-Packard warned the following week.

t: S&P 500 in a bear market; Nasdaq below 2,000
how: S&P 500 −4.3% to 1,180.16, 22.7% below its peak. Nasdaq −6.3%. The Dow lost 7.7% that week.
S&P 500 −2.4%, Nasdaq −4.8%. The third cut of the year was sold.
S&P 500 27.8% and Nasdaq 67.5% below their peaks. Next day Nasdaq +8.9% on Dell and Alcoa.
S&P 500 +3.9%, Nasdaq +8.1%. The Fed cited falling profits and investment. Cisco had warned two days earlier.
Up 19.0% from 4 April; the Nasdaq peaked a day later, up 41.2%. The S&P 500 fell 26.4% from here to 21 September.

t: JDS Uniphase: record write-down, 7,000 more jobs cut
how: Reported after the close on 26 July. JDSU −10%; the Nasdaq barely moved, by then numb to such news.

t: Markets reopen after 11 September; Fed cuts before the open
how: Closed for four trading days. Dow −7.1%, a record point loss; S&P 500 −4.9%; Nasdaq −6.8%.
Dow −14.3% on the week, its largest weekly loss since 1940. VIX intraday high of the bear market, 49.35. The S&P 500 then rose 21.4%.
Filed on Sunday 2 December, the largest US bankruptcy to that date. S&P 500 −0.8%; the market report did not mention it.
Up 21.4% and 44.7% from 21 September: the largest failed rally of the bear. The S&P 500 fell 33.8% from here.
Disclosed after the close on 25 June. The Dow fell 200 points early and closed −7. The slide into July followed.
Filed on Sunday 21 July. S&P 500 −3.3% to 819.83 after nine losing weeks.
S&P 500 −2.6%, first close under 800 since 1997. Volume and fear peaked in this stretch, eleven weeks before the final low.
Adelphia arrests and a deal in Congress on accounting reform. Dow +489. Another +5.4% followed on 29 July.
S&P 500 +0.4% to 902.78. The index had gained 13% in five sessions.

t: VIX closing peak of the bear market: 45.08
how: The Nasdaq closed below its July low. The VIX was lower, at 42.13, when the S&P 500 made its final low 46 sessions later.
Up 20.7% from 23 July on light volume. The index fell 19.3% from here to the low.
Dow −2.9% on bearish broker notes on GE and GM. S&P 500 −49.1% from its peak, 637 sessions after it.

t: Citigroup, GM, J&J beat forecasts: S&P 500 +4.7%
how: Fourth session after the low, on higher volume, after Yahoo (10 Oct) and GE (11 Oct). Dow +13.3% in four sessions.
S&P 500 +0.9%. The cut came four weeks after the low, with the index already up 19%.
Up 20.9% from 9 October; Nasdaq up 33.6%. A fall of 14.7% over three and a half months followed.
3.1% above the October low on low volume, with a UN vote on Iraq delayed. The Nasdaq was 14% above its October low.

t: S&P 500 +3.5% hours before the Iraq ultimatum
how: Fourth session after the retest low. The ultimatum came after the close and the invasion began on 20 March.

t: Fed cuts to 1.00%, its last cut
how: A smaller cut than some wanted: Dow −1.1%, S&P 500 −0.8%. The index was 26% above its October low.
